newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil policeman sentenced to 449 years for murders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil policeman sentenced to 449 years for murders.

text.p: A Brazilian judge sentenced a former policeman on Sunday to 449 years in prison for his role in an August 1993 massacre at a Rio de Janeiro slum in which 21 people died, authorities said.

Judge Jose Geraldo Antonio of Rio's Second Tribunal sentenced Paulo Roberto Alvarenga, 38, to 449 years and eight months after he was found guilty on 21 counts of murder and four counts of attempted murder, a court spokeswoman said.
Alvarenga was the first of 52 policemen to be tried in connection with the August 30, 1993, massacre at Vigario Geral, a Rio shanty town.
Alvarenga was named by witnesses as being one of 20 hooded gunmen who used automatic weapons and shotguns to mow down residents of the slum to avenge the deaths of four officers.
Despite Alvarenga's lenghty sentence, no one can serve more than 30 years for any crime under Brazilian law and many convicted murderers are released on parole long before then.
